title: Pending Home Sales Index (NAR, September 2026 data) — the first edition whose reference month is entirely post-decision, 10:00 a.m. ET inside the October FOMC blackout
source: IR: the publisher's own 2026 forward calendar — nar.realtor/press-releases/nar-statistical-news-release-schedule (HTTP 200, 483,177 bytes, fetched direct 2026-09-08) and its downloadable twin /sites/default/files/2025-11/2026-nar-statistical-news-release-schedule.docx (HTTP 200, 55,384 bytes, published 2025-11), whose 2026 table reads verbatim "Tue., Oct. 20 | September Pending Home Sales Index", one row below "Tue., Oct. 13 | September Existing-Home Sales". The two surfaces agree row for row across all nine remaining 2026 rows, and the .docx carries the standing note "All releases are distributed at 10 a.m. Eastern Time." Promoted from the `EST:` proposal filed 2026-09-08 by the pending-home-sales-2026-09-17 sweep, on the precedent pending-home-sales-2026-09-17, pending-home-sales-2026-12-17 and existing-home-sales-2026-11-12 already set: NAR PRODUCES this series rather than reporting someone else's, so its forward calendar is a primary source, and the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no closer member than `IR:`. PROMOTED ON EXECUTION, NOT ONLY ON SCHEDULE, and the execution record was re-derived independently this session rather than inherited: NAR's own sitemap (six paged sitemaps, all HTTP 200) carries exactly two 2026 PHSI releases, and both score exact against their scheduled rows to the day and the hour, read from the releases' own <time> elements — June data scheduled "Thu., July 16" published 2026-07-16T09:00:00-05:00, July data scheduled "Tue., Aug. 18" published 2026-08-18T09:01:00-05:00 (10:00 and 10:01 ET). n=2 is this surface's ceiling; older releases have rotated out. THE ONE CONFLICTING NAR SURFACE IS RECORDED, NOT HIDDEN, and it does not touch this edition: the pending-home-sales statistics page (HTTP 200, 565,623 bytes) still carries a stale next-release note naming the AUGUST edition on "Thursday, September 10, 2026" — the sibling series' date under this series' name, which the 09-17 lane established is a series-labelling error rather than a rival schedule. That page names no October date at all, so it contradicts nothing here; its 30-byte drift from the 2026-09-06 fetch is elsewhere in the page and the note itself is character-identical and still uncorrected. THIS ENTRY'S DATE CLAIM IS PRE-ADJUDICATED BY A SIBLING: FT-pending-home-sales-2026-09-17-1 scores the same governing-surface question on 2026-09-17, 33 days before this print, so a fail there reverts this entry to `estimate` with a month of warning. Registered here as FT-pending-home-sales-2026-10-20-1. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: The September edition of the series whose August (pending-home-sales-2026-09-17), November (pending-home-sales-2026-12-17) and October-data (pending-home-sales-2026-11-18) editions this calendar already tracks. WHAT MAKES THIS EDITION DIFFERENT FROM ITS SIBLING, AND IT IS AN INVERSION. PHSI counts contracts SIGNED, so the 09-17 print's August data predated the 2026-09-16 FOMC decision entirely and could contain no reaction to it; this print's SEPTEMBER reference month is the FIRST that sits wholly after that decision, so it is the first edition that can carry one. The session geometry inverts too: 09-17 was FOMC+1 and a September witching eve — maximum Fed noise — while 2026-10-20 sits INSIDE the October blackout (fomc-blackout-start-2026-10-17 is tracked; the decision is 2026-10-28, six sessions later, per federalreserve.gov) and two sessions after October opex (2026-10-16), which is close to the quietest Fed window a print can occupy. FOUR FINDINGS FROM THIS EVENT'S INITIAL RESEARCH (2026-09-08, D-42). (1) THE PRE-DECISION WIDENING THAT A SINGLE LAG APPEARS TO SHOW IS A MULTIPLE-COMPARISONS ARTIFACT. Testing ITB session range on each pre-decision lag -1..-12 over 103 FOMC decisions parsed from federalreserve.gov (2014+, permutation p at 20,000 iterations, baseline n=1,977), lag -6 reads 2.074% vs 1.836% (p=0.019) and lag -4 reads 2.053% (p=0.025) — but that is 2 of 12 nominal hits where 0.6 is expected by chance, neither survives a Bonferroni threshold of 0.0042, and the two hits are NON-ADJACENT with lag -5 null between them (p=0.252), which no real window effect produces. The honest aggregate is the window itself: the blackout slot (-5..-8) reads 1.844% vs 1.830%, p=0.684 — NULL. Had this lane tested only the lag 2026-10-20 actually occupies, it would have published a p=0.019 'blackout widening' that is not there. (2) THE BUILDER-EARNINGS COLLISION HAS DRIFTED OFF THIS SLOT WITHIN THE LAST FOUR YEARS. Re-run EDGAR 8-K Item 2.02 dates (caches busted 2026-09-08) show October is NVR's and PHM's quarter, not LEN's or KBH's, and NVR filed within +/-1 day of October 20 in 7 of its 14 October filings 2012-2025 (2013-10-21, 2014-10-20, 2015-10-20, 2016-10-20, 2017-10-19, 2020-10-20, 2021-10-21) — a slot collision far stronger than anything September offers. But NVR's filing has drifted later every year since 2022 (10-25, 10-24, 10-22, 10-22) and its FY2026 lag from quarter end is +22d (2026-04-22) and +23d (2026-07-23), pointing at ~10-22/10-23; PHM's is +23d/+22d, the same window; and DHI's October filing is its FISCAL-YEAR report, whose own lag is +29d/+28d (2024-10-29, 2025-10-28), pointing at ~10-28. So all three land AFTER the print, 2 to 6 sessions later. Registered as FT-pending-home-sales-2026-10-20-2. (3) THE 'POST-PEAK MORTGAGE RATE' READING THAT WOULD MAKE THIS PRINT A RECOVERY STORY IS FALSE ON THE PUBLISHED RATE PATH. NAR's own chief economist attributed July's -2.3% to 'the highest mortgage rates of the year... right in the middle of summer', but Freddie Mac's PMMS history (freddiemac.com/pmms/docs/PMMS_history.csv, HTTP 200, fetched 2026-09-08) shows July 2026 averaged 6.542%, August averaged 6.667%, and the first September print is 6.71% on 2026-09-03 — the HIGHEST weekly 30-year reading of 2026. September signings, this print's reference month, faced higher rates than the month NAR called the peak. Registered as FT-pending-home-sales-2026-10-20-3. (4) THE ATTRIBUTION STACK IS DENSER THAN 09-17's. Within 48 hours the corridor carries nahb-hmi-2026-10-19, housing-starts-2026-10-20 at 08:30 (ninety minutes before this print) and treasury-20y-bond-2026-10-21; existing-home-sales-2026-10-13 lands a week earlier and fhfa-hpi-2026-10-27 a week later. Impact stays `low` and `symbols: []`: no house playbook in docs/plans/trade-playbooks.md is macro- or housing-keyed, no instrument attaches, and the 12-17 lane measured this release class's own 10:00-11:00 hour indistinguishable from an ordinary hour on ITB (33.9% vs 35.3% of session range, 723 sessions, p=0.79). `confirmed` licenses nothing.
